page.overview:
Who is Shabbith-Ka?

Shabbith-Ka is a Lesser Outer God which appears in the H. P. Lovecraft-inspired Cthulhu Mythos. Created by Jeff Moeller, it appeared in the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game scenario "What Goes Around, Comes Around," first published in The Unspeakable Oath #8/9, and later included in the collection The Resurrected III: Out of the Vault.

Shabbith-Ka manifests as an amorphous blob of glowing purple energy; staring at the entity for long enough may allow the viewer to discern the outline of a rudimentary face, although what effect such an action might have on the person's sanity is enough to make one shudder.

The entity's worshippers summon it through the use of a particular spell, which is employed in the form of a song. When summoned, anyone not under the protection of an Elder Sign or actively singing the summoning spell will be attacked and consumed by it. It achieves this by absorbing the person into its "body," leaving nothing behind but a purple-tinged husk, which quickly disintegrates into ashes. Due to the nature of its form, physical weapons are useless against Shabbith-Ka.

When exposed to an Elder Sign, or if it has simply run out of viable prey, Shabbith-Ka retreats back to its lair at the centre of the universe, either by blasting through space at an incredible velocity or simply fading away into the void.
